title: Reliance Damages Retained Value Offset
subject: Contracts
stem:
The written service agreement gave Esther the right to operate a diagnostic-tool calibration booth at Luke's spring trade expo and required Luke to secure the electrical hookup and vendor permit. Before the expo opened, Luke repudiated. Esther cannot prove projected profits with reasonable certainty because the booth was her first attempt at that trade show and had no reliable sales history.

After the agreement was signed, Esther reasonably spent $18,600 leasing calibration benches, $7,400 on trade-expo mailers, and $6,200 on branded tool cases. The tool cases remain usable in a later calibration business and have a $2,700 remaining value.
call: What amount may Esther recover as reliance damages?

choices.B: $74,000, Esther's hoped-for profits from the trade expo.
choices.D: Nothing, because the projected profits are speculative.

rightExplanation: Esther may recover her reliance interest because Luke repudiated and her expected profits cannot be proved with reasonable certainty. Reliance damages compensate reasonable expenditures made in preparation for or performance of the contract, but they do not let the injured party keep value still retained. Esther reasonably spent $18,600, $7,400, and $6,200, for total expenditures of $32,200. The tool cases remain usable and have $2,700 in retained value. Subtracting that value leaves $29,500.

wrongExplanations.A: Adding all expenditures has the right reliance frame. The breaker is that retained value from reusable tool cases must be offset to avoid overcompensation.
wrongExplanations.D: Speculative profits make expectation damages unavailable. The breaker is that proven reliance expenditures can still be recovered even when profits are not reasonably certain.
wrongExplanations.B: The hoped-for trade-expo profits look like the benefit Esther expected. The breaker is that the facts say those profits cannot be proved with reasonable certainty.
